question: Should phase 2 be skipped when phase 1 is confident, and run only on low confidence or multiple/overlapping events?

q1_confidence_calibration.verdict: NOT CALIBRATED in the gating range; high bucket slightly worse than middle. No usable signal between 0.70 and 1.00.
q1_confidence_calibration.implication: A confidence gate would skip phase 2 on exactly the windows that need it most (W1 and W4).
q1_confidence_calibration.caveat: Only 4 items in the 0.70-0.89 bucket; the ordering is weak evidence, the confident-error list is not.

q2_phase2_value.verdict: Phase 2 changes the scored metric by exactly zero across all five post-fix runs.
q2_phase2_value.cross_ref: 051 showed the entire two-phase gain comes from multi-event DISCOVERY (a phase-1 capability), not from verification.

recommendation.confidence_gate: NO - uncalibrated; would skip verification on the worst errors
recommendation.router_on_event_count: Defensible as a structural trigger, but premature
recommendation.reasoning: Routing phase 2 to multi-event windows sends it where phase 1 already did the work. Before building a router to SOMETIMES skip phase 2, note the data already shows discovery-only scores identically at half the cost. A router is more machinery than a config flag for a decision already made. This is the project's own MINT principle.
recommendation.preferred: Make phase 2 a per-recipe flag: default off for throughput, on for human-reviewed work. Revisit when the reference set can resolve a 0.000 delta.
keep_phase2_for: potential_event routing to human review (W5 @0.49 correctly queued)
recommendation.note: Those are safety behaviours, not accuracy; they do not show in F1 on six labels.

blocking_constraint: With sd 0.100 and six positive labels, a real phase-2 effect of +/-0.05 would be invisible. Reference-set size gates this decision.
